Node.js builtins only, no external packages. ESM.\n\n`opts = {groupCol, valueCol, ops}`; `groupCol` and `valueCol` are column names from the header row; `ops` is an array drawn from `\"count\"`, `\"sum\"`, `\"min\"`, `\"max\"`, `\"mean\"`.\n\nParsing. Fields are separated by commas. A field may be wrapped in double quotes; a quote opens a quoted section only as the first character of a field. Inside a quoted section, a doubled quote (`\"\"`) is one literal quote character, a single quote closes the section, and commas, CR, LF, and CRLF lose their special meaning. After the closing quote, characters up to the next comma or line break are appended literally. A quote elsewhere in an unquoted field is a literal character. Line breaks may be LF, CRLF, or a lone CR, in any mix; CRLF counts as one line break. There are no other escape sequences. Rows are separated by a line break that is not inside a quoted section. Empty lines (a line break immediately followed by a line break, with nothing at all between them) are skipped wherever they appear; a line consisting only of `\"\"` or only of `,` is not empty and is a real row. The first non-empty line is the header row; if the input contains no non-empty line, there is no header row and the result is `[]`. The input may end with or without a trailing line break. A row with more or fewer fields than the header is malformed and is silently skipped. Leading and trailing whitespace of an unquoted field is NOT trimmed. Duplicate column names in the header are not special-cased; the first column with a given name wins.\n\nAggregation. `aggregate` returns an array of objects, one per distinct group value, in order of first appearance. Each result object has `group: <groupValue>` (the raw group string) plus one property per requested op, in the order the ops appear in `ops`. `count` may be requested like any other op and occupies the position it is given; an op omitted from `ops` has no property. `count` is the number of data rows in the group, including rows whose value fails to parse. The other ops aggregate over only the rows whose value parses as a finite number: `sum` (numeric total), `min`/`max` (extremes), `mean` (`Math.round(sum / n * 1000) / 1000`, `n` = parsed value count). Values are parsed with `Number(value.trim())`; an empty string, `NaN`, and infinities count as parse failures. When no row in the group has a parseable value: `sum` is `0`, `min`/`max`/`mean` are `null`. If `groupCol` or `valueCol` is not a header column name, the result is `[]`.\n"}],"timestamp":1794044406870}}

// count includes rows even if value fails to parse\n\n    if (num !== null && num !== undefined) {\n      // Guard: undefined stays as no contribution, null is a parse failure.\n      if (typeof num === \"number\" && Number.isFinite(num)) {\n        if (\"sum\" in entry) entry.sum += num;\n        if (\"min\" in entry) entry.min = entry.min === null ? num : Math.min(entry.min, num);\n        if (\"max\" in entry) entry.max = entry.max === null ? num : Math.max(entry.max, num);\n        if (\"mean\" in entry) entry._nNum = (entry._nNum || 0) + 1, entry._sumForMean = (entry._sumForMean || 0) + num;\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  const result = [];\n  for (const entry of groups.values()) {\n    if (\"mean\" in entry) {\n      if (entry._nNum == null || entry._nNum === 0) {\n        entry.mean = null;\n      } else {\n        entry.mean = Math.round((entry._sumForMean / entry._nNum) * 1000) / 1000;\n      }\n    }\n    const out = { group: entry.group };\n    for (const op of ops) {\n      if (op === \"count\") out.count = entry._n;\n      else if (op === \"sum\") out.sum = entry.sum;\n      else if (op === \"min\") out.min = entry.min;\n      else if (op === \"max\") out.max = entry.max;\n      else if (op === \"mean\") out.mean = entry.mean;\n    }\n    result.push(out);\n  }\n  return result;\n}\n\nfunction parseValue(raw) {\n  if (raw === undefined || raw === null) return null;\n  const trimmed = raw.trim();\n  if (trimmed === \"\") return null;\n  const n = Number(trimmed);\n  if (Number.isNaN(n) || !Number.isFinite(n)) return null;\n  return n;\n}\n\n// Parse CSV text into an array of rows (arrays of strings), skipping empty\n// lines and handling quoted sections per RFC 4180.\nfunction parseRows(text) {\n  const rows = [];\n  let field = \"\";\n  let row = [];\n  let fieldsEmpty = true; // is current row containing anything at all?\n  let inQuotes = false;\n  let i = 0;\n  const len = text.length;\n\n  // We track whether the row currently has any content (beyond \"already have an empty field\").\n  let rowHasContent = false;\n\n  while (i < len) {\n    const ch = text[i];\n\n    if (inQuotes) {\n      if (ch === '\"') {\n        if (text[i + 1] === '\"') {\n          field += '\"';\n          i += 2;\n        } else {\n          inQuotes = false;\n          i += 1;\n        }\n      } else {\n        field += ch;\n        if (ch === \"\\r\" || ch === \"\\n\") {\n          // inside quotes we may have literal newlines, but we handle whole text\n          // as one string; just add the char.\n        }\n        i += 1;\n      }\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    if (ch === '\"' && field === \"\" && (row.length === 0 || row[row.length - 1].startedQuote === undefined) && row.concat([field]).length > 0) {\n      // open quote only if this is first char of a field\n      // Simplest: track whether field is empty AND it's the start of field.\n    }\n\n    if (ch === '\"') {\n      // A quote opens a quoted section only as the first character of a field.\n      // \"First character of a field\" = the field's content so far is empty and\n      // we're at a position right after a comma or a line break (or start).\n      const atFieldStart = row.length === 0 && field.length === 0; // not reliable alone\n      // We need to know if we are at the start of a field:\n      // This is true if `field.length === 0` (we never appended to current field).\n      if (field.length === 0) {\n        inQuotes = true;\n        i += 1;\n      } else {\n        field += '\"';\n        i += 1;\n      }\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    if (ch === \",\") {\n      row.push(field);\n      if (field !== \"\" || rowHasContent) rowHasContent = true;\n      field = \"\";\n      i += 1;\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    if (ch === \"\\r\" || ch === \"\\n\") {\n      // line break\n      if (ch === \"\\r\" && text[i + 1] === \"\\n\") {\n        i += 2;\n      } else {\n        i += 1;\n      }\n      // end of row\n      row.push(field);\n      const rowHasAnything = rowHasContent || field !== \"\";\n      if (rowHasAnything) {\n        rows.push(row);\n      }\n      row = [];\n      field = \"\";\n      rowHasContent = false;\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    field += ch;\n    i += 1;\n  }\n\n  // trailing content (no trailing line break)\n  if (field !== \"\" || rowHasContent || row.length >= 0) {\n    // Only add a final row if there's anything meaningful. Tracks whether any content\n// character was seen so empty lines can be skipped. A field that is `\"\"`\n// counts as content; a line of only commas counts as content.\nfunction parseOneRecord(text, start, len) {\n  const fields = [];\n  let field = \"\";\n  let inQuotes = false;\n  let i = start;\n  let sawContent = false; // the `\"\"` field is real content\n        i += 1;\n      } else {\n        field += '\"'; // literal quote in the middle of a field\n        sawContent = true;\n        i += 1;\n      }\n      continue;\n    }\n    if (ch === \",\") {\n      fields.push(field);\n      field = \"\";\n      sawContent = true; A field that is `\"\"`\n// counts as content; a line of only commas counts as content.\nfunction parseOneRecord(text, start, len) {\n  const fields = [];\n  let field = \"\";\n  let inQuotes = false;\n  let i = start;\n  let sawContent = false; // any real character (or quote) seen in this record\n  let recordEnded = false;\n\n  while (i < len) {\n    const ch = text[i];\n\n    if (inQuotes) {\n      if (ch === '\"') {\n        if (text[i + 1] === '\"') {\n          field += '\"';\n          i += 2;\n        } else {\n          inQuotes = false;\n          i += 1;\n        }\n      } else {\n        field += ch;\n        i += 1;\n      }\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    if (ch === '\"') {\n      // A quote opens a quoted section only as the first character of a field.\n      if (field.length === 0) {\n        inQuotes = true;\n        sawContent = true; // the `\"\"` field is real content\n        i += 1;\n      } else {\n        field += '\"'; // literal quote in the middle of a field\n        sawContent = true;\n        i += 1;\n      }\n      continue;\n    }\n    if (ch === \",\") {\n      fields.push(field);\n      field = \"\";\n      sawContent = true; // a comma implies real field structure\n      i += 1;\n      continue;\n    }\n    if (ch === \"\\r\" || ch === \"\\n\") {\n      // line break ends the record (CRLF counts as one)\n      if (ch === \"\\r\" && text[i + 1] === \"\\n\") i += 2;\n      else i += 1;\n      fields.push(field);\n      field = \"\";\n      recordEnded = true;\n      break;\n    }\n    field += ch;\n    sawContent = true;\n    i += 1;\n  }\n\n  if (!recordEnded) {\n    fields.push(field);\n  }\n\n  return { fields, nextIndex: i, isEmpty: !sawContent };\n}"}]},"isError":false}

Node.js builtins only, no external packages. ESM.\n\n`opts = {groupCol, valueCol, ops}`; `groupCol` and `valueCol` are column names from the header row; `ops` is an array drawn from `\"count\"`, `\"sum\"`, `\"min\"`, `\"max\"`, `\"mean\"`.\n\nParsing. Fields are separated by commas. A field may be wrapped in double quotes; a quote opens a quoted section only as the first character of a field. Inside a quoted section, a doubled quote (`\"\"`) is one literal quote character, a single quote closes the section, and commas, CR, LF, and CRLF lose their special meaning. After the closing quote, characters up to the next comma or line break are appended literally. A quote elsewhere in an unquoted field is a literal character. Line breaks may be LF, CRLF, or a lone CR, in any mix; CRLF counts as one line break. There are no other escape sequences. Rows are separated by a line break that is not inside a quoted section. Empty lines (a line break immediately followed by a line break, with nothing at all between them) are skipped wherever they appear; a line consisting only of `\"\"` or only of `,` is not empty and is a real row. The first non-empty line is the header row; if the input contains no non-empty line, there is no header row and the result is `[]`. The input may end with or without a trailing line break. A row with more or fewer fields than the header is malformed and is silently skipped. Leading and trailing whitespace of an unquoted field is NOT trimmed. Duplicate column names in the header are not special-cased; the first column with a given name wins.\n\nAggregation. `aggregate` returns an array of objects, one per distinct group value, in order of first appearance. Each result object has `group: <groupValue>` (the raw group string) plus one property per requested op, in the order the ops appear in `ops`. `count` may be requested like any other op and occupies the position it is given; an op omitted from `ops` has no property. `count` is the number of data rows in the group, including rows whose value fails to parse. The other ops aggregate over only the rows whose value parses as a finite number: `sum` (numeric total), `min`/`max` (extremes), `mean` (`Math.round(sum / n * 1000) / 1000`, `n` = parsed value count). Values are parsed with `Number(value.trim())`; an empty string, `NaN`, and infinities count as parse failures. When no row in the group has a parseable value: `sum` is `0`, `min`/`max`/`mean` are `null`. If `groupCol` or `valueCol` is not a header column name, the result is CSV aggregator: parse RFC 4180-style CSV and compute grouped aggregates.\nexport function aggregate(csvText, opts) {\n  const headers = parseRows(csvText);\n  if (headers.length === 0) return [];\n  const header = headers[0];\n  const rows = headers.slice(1);\n\n  const { groupCol, valueCol, ops } = opts;\n\n  const groupIdx = header.indexOf(groupCol);\n  const valueIdx = header.indexOf(valueCol);\n  if (groupIdx === -1 || valueIdx === -1) return [];\n\n  // Maps preserve insertion order in JS.\n  const groups = new Map();\n\n  for (const row of rows) {\n    if (row.length !== header.length) continue;\n    const groupVal = row[groupIdx];\n    const num = parseValue(row[valueIdx]);\n\n    if (!groups.has(groupVal)) {\n      const entry = { group: groupVal };\n      for (const op of ops) {\n        if (op === \"count\") {\n          entry.count = 0;\n        } else if (op === \"sum\") {\n          entry.sum = 0;\n        } else if (op === \"min\") {\n 0;\n      groups.set(groupVal, entry);\n    }\n\n    const entry = groups.get(groupVal);\n    entry._n += 1; // count includes rows even if value fails to parse\n\n    if (num !== null && num !== undefined) {\n      // Guard: undefined stays as no contribution, null is a parse failure.\n      if (typeof num === \"number\" && Number.isFinite(num)) {\n        if (\"sum\" in entry) entry.sum += num;\n        if (\"min\" in entry) entry.min = entry.min === null ? num : Math.min(entry.min, num);\n        if (\"max\" in entry) entry.max = entry.max === null ? num : Math.max(entry.max, num);\n        if (\"mean\" in entry) entry._nNum = (entry._nNum || 0) + 1, entry._sumForMean = (entry._sumForMean || 0) + num;\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  const result = [];\n  for (const entry of / entry._nNum) * 1000) / 1000;\n      }\n    }\n    const out = { group: entry.group };\n    for (const op of ops) {\n      if (op === \"count\") out.count = entry._n;\n      else if (op === \"sum\") out.sum = entry.sum;\n      else if (op === \"min\") out.min = entry.min;\n      else if (op === \"max\") out.max = entry.max;\n      else if (op === \"mean\") out.mean = entry.mean;\n    }\n    result.push(out);\n  }\n  return result;\n}\n\nfunction parseValue(raw) {\n  if (raw === undefined || raw === null) return null;\n  const trimmed = raw.trim();\n  if (trimmed === \"\") return null;\n  const n = Number(trimmed);\n  if (Number.isNaN(n) || !Number.isFinite(n)) return null;\n  return n;\n}\n\n// Parse CSV text into an array of rows (arrays of strings), skipping empty\n// lines and handling quoted sections per RFC 4180.\nfunction parseRows(text) {\n  const rows = [];\n  let field = \"\";\n  let row = [];\n  let fieldsEmpty = true; // is current row containing anything at all?\n  let inQuotes = false;\n  let i = 0;\n  const len = text.length;\n\n  // We track whether the row currently has any content (beyond \"already have an empty field\").\n  let rowHasContent = false;\n\n  while (i < len) {\n    const ch = text[i];\n\n    if (inQuotes) {\n      if (ch === '\"') {\n        if (text[i + 1] === '\"') {\n          field += '\"';\n          i += 2;\n        } else {\n          inQuotes = false;\n          i += 1;\n        }\n      } else {\n        field += ch;\n        if (ch === \"\\r\" || ch === \"\\n\") {\n          // inside quotes we may have literal newlines, but
